description: THE COMBINED-REVISION GOLDEN (M17, product audit 2026-08-14, docs/design/topological-naming.md §12a). A 100x40 plate, 14 mm thick, with a Ø30 central bore and two mounting holes on its top (+Z) face: Ø7 at (18, 20) and Ø6.6 at (82, 20). The tree is stored in exactly the state a document is left in after TWO ordinary edits — Hole1's diameter was retyped 6.6 -> 7, and then Extrude1's distance 10 -> 14 — so every stored face signature still says z = 10, AND Hole2's stored signature still describes the face as it was when Hole1 was Ø6.6 (centroid x = 50.335933053394236, area 3258.929708944704 mm^2, the audit's own numbers to 4 dp). Neither edit alone breaks anything: at constant thickness the tier-2 coplanar re-match absorbs the stale area, and with no diameter edit the tier-3 translated re-match absorbs the moved plane. TOGETHER they defeated all three tiers and the audit measured 4 of 11 features red on this shape — the P0 this golden locks. Hole2 resolves through the tier-4 enclosing re-match (geometry.kernel.faces.enclosing_face_match), whose anchor is the face's OUTER boundary, the one invariant an interior hole edit cannot touch. Note the stored centroid it re-anchors from is INSIDE the Ø30 bore, i.e. not on the face at all, which is why the containment test is against the outer boundary and not against the face.
derivation: Three through-bores removed, each the full 14 mm depth: pi*14*(15^2 + 3.5^2 + 3.3^2) = pi*14*248.14 = 3473.96*pi mm^3.

Surface area: plate faces 2*(100*40) + 2*(100*14) + 2*(40*14) = 11920 mm^2; the top and bottom faces each lose the three discs pi*248.14, so -496.28*pi; the three bores add lateral cylinders 2*pi*14*(15 + 3.5 + 3.3) = 610.4*pi. Area = 11920 + 114.12*pi = 12278.518553627668 mm^2 (measured deviation 0.0).

Centroid: y = 20 and z = 7 by symmetry (all three bores sit on the plate's y centreline and run its full depth). x is NOT 50 and that is the point of the part: the two mounting holes are symmetric about x = 50 in POSITION but not in SIZE (Ø7 at x=18 against Ø6.6 at x=82), so the x centroid is a single number that moves the moment either hole is drilled anywhere but at its picked station. x = (56000*50 - 14*pi*(225*50 + 12.25*18 + 10.89*82)) / (56000 - 3473.96*pi) = 50.04245441354795 mm (measured deviation 2.1e-14).

AABB unchanged by the bores: (0,0,0)-(100,40,14). As the sibling revision golden notes, a hole drilled from the STALE z=10 plane would still reach the bottom under through_all, so the bbox alone cannot catch a mis-anchored drill — the x centroid can, and does.
Topology: 6 plate planar faces + 3 cylindrical bore faces = 9 faces; 12 plate edges + 3 per bore (top circle, bottom circle, cylindrical seam) = 21 edges; 1 shell.

Mesh (linear_deflection 0.1): 1542 vertices / 1536 triangles. INDEPENDENTLY CROSS-CHECKED rather than recorded: the same tree with all three face signatures and hole positions authored at the CURRENT state (centroid z = 14, Hole2's face described with Hole1 already at Ø7 — a tier-1 STRICT match that never reaches any resilient tier) produces byte-identical GLB (sha256 85563175ea7ffad3...), identical topology, identical mesh counts and identical mass properties. So the tier-4 rescue lands on exactly the body an exact re-pick would have made, which is the claim this golden exists to make.
tolerance_rationale: Every bore is a pure boolean cut of a right cylinder from a box, so GProp integrates the analytic quadrics exactly; measured deviation from the closed forms above is 7.3e-12 mm^3 (volume), 0.0 mm^2 (area) and 2.1e-14 mm (centroid) — machine precision. The 1e-9 ceiling matches the sibling revise-thickness-hole-on-moved-face-60x40x16 and hole-through-r5-40x25x10 goldens and the kernel's 1e-7 m linear posture; it is 2-3 orders of magnitude above the observed residual and orders of magnitude below any mis-anchoring this golden exists to catch (drilling Hole2 at the face's area centroid, x = 50.37838219699429, instead of at its picked station moves the part's x centroid by 3.4e-1 mm, eight orders of magnitude outside it).
